chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, mentioned it, saying:

When Al-Mutawakkil was bitten (by a snake), he vowed that if he was healed, he would give a large amount of wealth in charity. When he was healed, he asked the jurists about the limit of 'a large amount', so they differed regarding it. Some of them said 'one hundred thousand', and some of them said 'ten thousand'. They gave differing opinions about it, so the matter became confused for him.

So a man from his courtiers, called Saf'an, said, 'Why don't you send to this blackie to ask him?' Al-Mutawakkil said to him, 'Whom do you mean, woe be unto you!' He said to him, 'Ibn al-Rida.' He said to him, 'And is he better than this thing?' He said, 'If he takes you out of this dilemma, then such and such is for me upon you, or else whip me one hundred lashes.'

Al-Mutawakkil said, 'I am pleased. O Ja'far ibn Mahmoud, go to him and ask him about the limit of 'a large amount'. So Ja'far ibn Mahmoud went to Abu Al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) and asked him about the limit of 'a large amount'. He said, 'The large amount is eighty.'

Ja'far said to him, 'O my master, he will ask me about the reason for it.' Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "Certainly, Allah helped you in many places" - so we counted those places and they were eighty.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a 'large amount' of wealth for charity according to Imam Ali ibn Muhammad (AS) in this hadith?
ai.summary: This narrative from Al-Kafi illustrates the Shia scholarly tradition of deriving legal definitions from Quranic exegesis, where Imam Ali ibn Muhammad (AS) links the concept of 'abundance' (al-kathir) to the number eighty based on the phrase 'many places' (mawatin kathira) in Surah Al-Anfal. The story highlights the Caliph's reliance on the Ahl al-Bayt for authoritative clarification amidst juristic disagreement, emphasizing the Imam's unique ability to uncover hidden numerical meanings (ta'wil) within the Quranic text.
